name: Introduction to Research Methodology and Communication in Mathematics
description:
Unit 1: Research Foundations and Ethics
Definition, concepts, and overview of research; approaches to research including basic, applied, interdisciplinary, and multidisciplinary research. Ethical principles in research: ethical reasoning in scientific practice, scientific conduct, intellectual honesty, responsible authorship, and proper citation and attribution. Research integrity: plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, and redundant publications, including duplication, overlapping publications, and salami slicing. Good research practices: data management, transparency, reproducibility, and conflicts of interest.
Unit 2: Foundations of Mathematical and Statistical Reasoning
Reasoning and Proof Techniques:
Mathematical statements and logic; necessary and sufficient conditions; contrapositive, converse, and negation; direct and indirect proofs; proof by contradiction; principle of mathematical induction; counterexamples; Axiom of Choice and Zorn’s Lemma; inductive and deductive reasoning.
Mathematical Modelling and Numerical Analysis:
Mathematical modelling and problem formulation; analytical and numerical solutions; approximations and error analysis; interpretation of analytical and computational results.
Statistical Reasoning and Data Analysis:
Data collection and sampling methods; data analysis and visualization; statistical hypothesis testing; introduction to statistical software, including SPSS, R, and Python-based tools.
Unit 3: Research Databases, Metrics, and Scientific Writing
Research Databases and Indexing Platforms:
Indexing and citation databases, including Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, MathSciNet, and zbMATH Open; search strategies; citation networks; and understanding indexed literature.
Research Metrics and Evaluation Indicators:
Journal-level metrics such as Impact Factor, CiteScore, SNIP, SJR, and IPP; author-level metrics including h-index, g-index, and i10-index; article-level metrics and altmetrics; scope and limitations of research metrics.
Scientific Writing, Documentation, and Publication Ethics:
LaTeX for documentation and Beamer presentations; reference management tools such as Mendeley and JabRef; bibliographic styles and citation formats; plagiarism and similarity checks; intellectual property rights and copyrights; preprints (arXiv), open access, and publication models.
Responsible Use of AI Tools in Mathematical Research:
Introduction to AI-assisted search, literature exploration, and scientific writing; appropriate use of AI for summarisation, LaTeX assistance, and bibliographic support, with emphasis on verification of mathematical content, academic integrity, and ethical considerations.
